Set up Eyrie for the first time: With no config yet, every page leads to the setup wizard: pick the tools, the folders you work in and a tasks file, review, save. The config file is checked on disk afterwards.
See what needs me at a glance: The home page: what needs attention, running sessions, the last week's spend, tasks and your setup.
See every running session, mine and Eyri: Sessions Eyrie runs in its own tmux, the Claude Code and Codex sessions open in your own terminals, and recent conversations you can resume.
Start a Claude Code session and type int: Starts a session from the New session dialog, opens its terminal in the browser, types a line and sees the reply, then stops it. Uses a stand-in claude script and a private tmux server; nothing real is launched.
Check what my agents cost: Usage across Claude Code and Codex at list prices: totals, the daily chart, by model and by project, for 30 and then 7 days.
Switch to dark mode and read usage: The theme toggle in the top bar, and the usage charts and tables in dark mode.
See which MCP servers each tool has: MCP servers configured for Claude Code (user scope) and Codex, read from their own config files.
See my Claude Code plugins: Installed plugins with their enabled state, from `claude plugin list`.
Read and edit what a subagent remembers: Opens a subagent's memory file, appends a line, saves, and checks the file on disk changed by exactly that line.
Tick off a task: Ticks a task on the Tasks page and checks only that line of the markdown file changed.
Review my settings: The Settings page shows what setup chose, and saving writes the config file.
Glance at the top-bar widget: The menu-bar widget's panel at its real size, reading the same summary as the home page. Desktop only.
